ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two triangles in the figure. The triangle on the left is labeled ABC, side AB is labeled x, and the base BC is labeled 5; there is one arc mark at angle A, and there are two arc marks at angle B. The triangle on the right is labeled EFD, side ED is labeled x−4, and side EF is labeled 3; there is one arc mark at angle D, and there are two arc marks at angle E. Reasoning: From the angle marks, it can be known that ∠A and ∠D are equal, and ∠B and ∠E are equal, so triangle ABC and triangle D E F are similar by AA. The correspondence is A↔D, B↔E, C↔F, so the corresponding sides are AB↔DE, BC↔EF. Thus AB/DE = BC/EF, that is, x/(x−4)=5/3. Cross-multiplying gives 3x=5x−20, so 2x=20, x=10. DE is required, and DE=x−4=10−4=6.
